title: A Beautiful Day
subtitle: When light strikes these films, silver halide undergoes a structural change, forming silver grains.

items.text: A Beautiful Day
In the days that follow, Jones's mood seems to perk up.
She asks Bette to read the newspaper to her, take pictures of the park, and even turn the glass chamber so she could bask in the sun.

items.speaker: Jones
items.text: In winter, we'd set the snow up into different piles, pick a few, and sprinkle sugar on them.
Sometimes, they just talk like old friends.

items.speaker: Jones
items.text: If we were lucky, we'd get a sweet one. If not, we might end up eating sawdust.

items.speaker: Bette
items.text: You played games like that as a kid?

items.speaker: Jones
items.text: Silly girl.
Jones lets out a weak chuckle.

items.speaker: Jones
items.text: Before I became famous, I was just a little country girl.

items.speaker: Bette
items.text: Hm?
Bette feels a twinge of something unfamiliar.

items.speaker: Jones
items.text: What's happening?
Bette shakes her head.

items.speaker: Bette
items.text: When I was little, I used to sneak into the cinema. It was crowded, but at least it was warm.

items.speaker: Bette
items.text: I loved watching movies. They let me forget the bad things in real life for a while ...

items.speaker: Bette
items.text: I felt like ... they were saving my numb little heart.

items.speaker: Bette
items.text: That's why I wanted to make movies—because I wanted to be one of those people.

items.speaker: Jones
items.text: Hmm ...
Jones watches Bette, a hint of resignation on her face.

items.speaker: Jones
items.text: Then, we need to make a movie.

items.speaker: Bette
items.text: Now?

items.speaker: Jones
items.text: We have a camera, don't we? Just letting it sit there is a waste.

items.speaker: Bette
items.text: What are we filming?
Jones smiles.

items.speaker: Jones
items.text: You.

items.speaker: Jones
items.text: Follow Bette. Medium shot. Upper body.
At Jones's command, the insect-like base carrying the camera moves toward Bette, angling the lens at her.
The device has been modified to respond to her commands.
Even confined to the glass chamber, Jones can still direct the shots she wants.

items.speaker: Bette
items.text: What's there to film about me?

Bette looks down with a red face at the camera as it tracks her. It feels so much different from when she had been a stunt double—the lens is capturing the real her now, and she doesn't handle it well.

items.speaker: Jones
items.text: Better than filming me in this state.
Jones shrugs.

items.speaker: Jones
items.text: Now, don't just stand there staring at it. Do your thing.

items.speaker: Bette
items.text: My thing?

items.speaker: Jones
items.text: You know ... something. Why not read me the newspaper?
Bette nods, grabs the paper, and sits beside Jones.
She begins reading, stumbling at first over simple words. But slowly she finds herself focusing on the text, not the camera, and begins to relax.

items.speaker: Jones
items.text: That's it. A good actor forgets the camera is even there.

items.speaker: Bette
items.text: Camera?!
She has indeed forgotten it, and all her nerves return as soon as she looks back at it, her face turning a new and brighter red.

items.speaker: Jones
items.text: Don't worry. You'll get used to it.
From then on, whenever Bette enters Jones's room, the camera soon turns to meet her.
And as per Jones's request, Bette edits their clips every night.
"Click."
In the dim red room, the sound of scissors cuts through a busy silence as Bette trims another frame of film.

items.speaker: Bette
items.text: And ... this frame next ...
She draws a line on the back of the film with a pencil, then carefully snips it out with scissors.
Setting the film aside, she draws large, bold letters on a piece of paper.

items.speaker: Bette
items.text: "Apple Core."
Bette had peeled an apple for Jones, only to be ruthlessly teased for her knife skills.

items.speaker: Bette
items.text: "Pharaoh's Night."
A horror-style short Jones had asked Bette to shoot, where Jones, wrapped head to toe in bandages, bolted upright in bed—
Only for the shot to reveal Bette's fake mustache stuck under her nose.
The last clip is of Bette laughing so hard the whole frame trembles, the light shifting wildly, like ink dispersing in a glass of water.

items.speaker: Bette
items.text: This is what movies should be ... magical vessels to preserve our best moments forever ...
She carefully lifts the film with tweezers, sorting them into separate categories.

items.speaker: Bette
items.text: Jones will recover and be discharged soon.

items.speaker: Bette
items.text: I'll find a way to help her accept what happened with the "Storm."
Bette's eyes rest overlong on the script on the nightstand—copied out laboriously by hand and from memory. Having used her legs as a writing desk for so long, the pages have developed a slight curve.

items.speaker: Bette
items.text: Then we'll finish the movie.
It is late, and the room is dark except for the intermittent flickering of machine lights.

items.speaker: Laura
items.text: Have you decided?

items.speaker: Jones
items.text: Yes.
The insect-like camera base sits motionless, slumped over from lack of instructions.

items.speaker: Jones
items.text: I don't need money. I just need you to give me one thing.

items.speaker: Laura
items.text: What?
Jones parts her lips, uttering something far from pleasant.

items.speaker: Laura
items.text: Hah! There are better substitutes for that.

items.speaker: Jones
items.text: Suit yourself.
The door shuts behind the nurse as she leaves.
